name: Fe-rich basalt, as MGS-1, a Mars regolith simulant
paper: J. Martikainen, O. Muñoz, T. Jardiel, J. C. Gómez Martín, M. Peiteado, Y. Willame, A. Penttilä, K. Muinonen, G. Wurm and T. Becker, "Optical constants of Martian dust analogs at UV–visible–near-infrared wavelengths", Astrophys. J. Suppl. 268 (2023) 47, DOI 10.3847/1538-4365/acf0be
source: the article's machine-readable Table 6, https://iopscience.iop.org/0067-0049/268/2/47/suppdata/apjsacf0bet6_ascii.txt?doi=10.3847/1538-4365/acf0be, SHA-256 a5ed6861dba6eb68aa310936854a29b1c772687fc4b4634ef8321dec3f806cd3, fetched 2026-10-14, its MGS-1 column; read as data
licence: Adapted from CC BY 4.0 material (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/): J. Martikainen et al., Astrophys. J. Suppl. 268 (2023) 47. Changed: MGS-1's k from Table 6 reduced onto this grid, with n the paper's fixed 1.5; this file is offered under CC BY 4.0
reduction: n linear and k linear in log k in wavelength between the source's rows, onto 380–780 nm every 5 nm, to six significant figures. Table 6's k is MGS-1's, retrieved with the paper's second Gaussian-random-sphere shapes and n fixed at 1.5; its 650 nm value, 4.33 × 10⁻⁴, is the index Martikainen et al. 2025's MGS-1 database takes (R08.T5.c's fidelity test), where Table 3's first shapes give 3.15 × 10⁻⁴. The rows are every 25 nm to 400 nm, then every 50 nm; the sample is a laboratory simulant at room temperature, unstated
standIn: a Mars regolith simulant stands in for Fe-rich basalt: MGS-1's absorption, retrieved by Martikainen et al. 2023 with its real index fixed at 1.5, since no open visible index of an Fe-rich basalt was found
